title: Flow receives a typed notice for every flow running on changed belief
description: At immutable belief-nexus 39b422e, Belief has no Flow concept or peer edge and never tells Flow which running flows hold old belief. Changed reaches subscribers only. Audit: /home/li/primary/flows/b862a0/audits/belief-nexus-v1-review.md, lines 20-26, 196-199, 330-333. This is an integration contract with Mind versionOne, not a local patch. It is first-launch priority; no repair is authorized now.
design: Design is pending the Mind beliefNexus Primary in coordination with Mind versionOne Secondary. At first launch, judge the smallest typed edge by which Belief reports successful changed-belief publication and Flow maps the affected workspace identities to running flows. Keep Belief ownership, workspace identity, publication completion, and Flow identity in their own contexts. Do no repair until the Primary settles which contract owns the mapping and acknowledgement.
acceptance_criteria: An agreed typed Belief–Flow contract is present in the responsible signal/library ethos and implemented by both repositories. A detached integration proof launches at least two flows whose workspaces use different belief sets, changes one used module, completes atomic refurnish, and shows Flow receives exactly the identities of the flows now running on old belief; the unaffected flow is absent. A failed refurnish produces no old-belief success notice. Restart/reconnect behavior is defined and tested so a delivered or recoverable notice cannot silently disappear. Nix checks pass in Belief and Flow.

title: Owner-scoped repositories, furnishing, and subscriptions preserve caller boundaries
description: First postlaunch judgment. At immutable belief-nexus 39b422e, ownership is not consistently scoped per caller. Audit: /home/li/primary/flows/b862a0/audits/belief-nexus-v1-review.md, lines 28-45, 169-185. Evidence grade — EXECUTED, temporary detached deployment: Login Register=Registered; Peer Resolve/Register=NotAuthorized; Peer Furnish=NotReady, so dynamic cross-owner publication is INCONCLUSIVE. STATIC: Furnish core reads all repository snapshots; subscription admission checks the owner, while state and event drain are unfiltered. This bead records the exact boundary to judge at first launch; no repair is authorized now.
design: Design is pending the Mind beliefNexus Primary. Treat this as first-launch priority. The design must make repository resolution, furnishing, current subscription state, and subsequent subscription events one coherent owner-scoped domain, while retaining typed peer admission. Do no repair until the Primary judges the intended owner relationship between login and Flow peer.
acceptance_criteria: A detached executable proof at immutable successor revisions establishes exact cross-owner negatives: after owner A registers repository A, owner B cannot resolve A modules, cannot furnish any A module into B workspace, cannot receive A workspace in subscription state, and cannot receive A events; B can independently register, resolve, furnish, and subscribe to repository B. The proof distinguishes NotAuthorized from readiness/configuration failures and exercises a successful publication path so the furnish boundary is conclusive. Same-owner Register, Resolve, Furnish, and Subscribe remain successful. Static review confirms every snapshot scan, workspace selection, state construction, and event drain is owner-filtered. Nix checks pass.

title: Belief file mock proves register resolve furnish
description: Build the file-backed Belief Nexus v1 proof. Register a repository and watch its main revision; Resolve names into found and missing; Furnish Codex workspaces with a model_instructions_file bundle for Spirit and Intent and .agents/skills for every other Kind; Subscribe and push Changed only after successful automatic atomic re-furnish. Removed and restored modules re-furnish automatically. Ambiguous module sources preserve the currently furnished workspace. Ordinary and meta paths use authenticated direct typed peer tests, caller ownership, configured peer lists, coherent configuration revision, and typed failure evidence. Prove a real Codex start discovers the generated bundle and skills. Package and prove the system with Nix.
design: Implement the complete typed ordinary and meta wire contracts first, then the Nexus, translators, repository watcher, atomic workspace generation, and subscriptions. Placement follows Kind. Every configuration field is set atomically through the responsible Nexus or Translator surface and carries one coherent revision. Bootstrap is typed. Peer access is authenticated against configured identities and direct typed peer tests exercise it. A repository main change is resolved as one candidate snapshot; only an unambiguous valid candidate replaces generated output, and Changed names successful workspaces after refurnish. Use Nix-native checks and a live Codex discovery proof.
acceptance_criteria: CLI proves Register, Resolve with one found and one missing name, Furnish into a temporary Codex workspace at model_instructions_file and .agents/skills, Subscribe/Changed, and automatic atomic re-furnish after module removal and restoration. Ambiguity leaves the current furnished workspace byte-identical. Typed failures carry evidence. Authenticated direct typed peer tests prove caller ownership and peer-list enforcement. A real Codex start reads the generated instructions and discovers the skill. Typed bootstrap and coherent per-field Nexus/Translator configuration are tested. Nix builds and runs the full proof.
notes: Supersedes the earlier placement:SystemPrompt|Skill proposal: placement is derived from source-folder Kind. Spirit and Intent go to the system-prompt bundle; all other Kinds go to skills.
close_reason: Proven at 234143836c372a6ed6b8ea561b54548aa2687db8 from a clean detached worktree: nix check passed; packaged belief-pair started from typed Place; public named belief-nexus-meta Configure None reached Ready; public named belief-nexus registered committed main and furnished separate Codex and Claude workspaces with absent-frontmatter Kind defaults plus explicit opposite default override; real codex exec and claude --print each returned BUNDLE_DEFAULT_TOKEN, BUNDLE_OVERRIDE_TOKEN, and SKILL_DEFAULT_TOKEN. Typed tests prove direct configured peer Furnish, unconfigured refusal, PeerId/Login ownership, found/missing, subscriptions/watch/refurnish, ambiguity preservation, durable recovery, and atomic publication.

title: Remaining deployment, meta, polling, retention, and type findings receive bounded dispositions
description: At immutable belief-nexus 39b422e, the audit records a bounded remainder across deployment/Place and XDG behavior, meta subscription and dead MetaPeers, polling cost, retention/event history, translator outcomes, and strings or made-up values where the vision calls for types. Audit: /home/li/primary/flows/b862a0/audits/belief-nexus-v1-review.md, lines 115-132, 219-328, 343-350. This is a triage boundary, explicitly not an omnibus rewrite and not authorization to repair any finding now.
design: Design is pending the Mind beliefNexus Primary and is judged after first-launch priorities. Review each cited finding independently against the current short-term vision and runtime evidence. Record one of: accept as the v1 design, remove as unnecessary machinery, or create one narrowly scoped successor bead with its own contract and proof. Keep deployment, meta configuration, polling, retention, translator outcomes, and domain typing separate; do not braid them into one implementation change.
acceptance_criteria: A Primary-reviewed disposition table covers every finding in audit lines 115-132, 219-328, and 343-350 exactly once, with evidence, vision basis, and one of accepted, removal, or a single-purpose successor bead. Deployment/Place and XDG, meta configuration/subscription/MetaPeers, polling work at rest, generation retention and event history, typed translator outcome, external-call command typing, location correctness, and string/made-up-value typing each have an explicit disposition. Any successor bead has one bounded outcome, design, and executable acceptance proof; dependencies state ordering without forming an omnibus rewrite. This triage bead changes no runtime code. Its exported bead state is committed and the repository remains clean.

title: Belief Library, Memory, and Operation ethos describe the implemented Nexus path
description: At immutable belief-nexus 39b422e, Signal and Emission have ethos, while the shared Library, persistent Memory, and Operation attempts are absent as ethos specifications. Shared types instead live in Signal; MemoryImage and Daemon methods are handwritten and substantially exceed the vision records. Audit: /home/li/primary/flows/b862a0/audits/belief-nexus-v1-review.md, lines 69-82, 134-167, 330-338. This bead asks for correspondence between declared anatomy and the chosen implementation, not syntax-shaped documentation. No repair is authorized now.
design: Design is pending the Mind beliefNexus Primary and is judged after first-launch priorities. First decide the actual minimal Library, Memory, and Operation ontology against the complete four-part Nexus concept; then make each implemented type and attempt belong to that ontology. Separate durable domain records from recovery machinery and derive or compile-check correspondence wherever ethos-zero can express it. Do no repair or hand-copy of Rust shapes into ethos before that judgment.
acceptance_criteria: Library ethos declares each shared type once and Signal, Operation, Memory, and Emission import it. Operation ethos has one attempt per ordinary input and a typed outcome for each path. Memory ethos declares the durable records actually needed for repositories, workspaces/publications, configuration, recovery, and successful-or-failed changes; transient process state is absent. Generated code or compile-time checks prove the Rust implementation bears the declared associations and that no duplicate contract-local definition remains. The four ethos files together trace Register, Resolve, Furnish, Subscribe, watch/refurnish, and failure paths from input through attempt and Memory to output/emission. Ethos generation checks and Nix checks pass.

title: Changed coherently names changed modules and successfully refurnished affected workspaces
description: At immutable belief-nexus 39b422e, every plan records every repository revision, so a move can refurnish unrelated workspaces. Changed is emitted once before refurnish with no workspaces and again per workspace with no modules; retry chooses the first repository in a pending basis. Audit: /home/li/primary/flows/b862a0/audits/belief-nexus-v1-review.md, lines 47-67, 187-199, 301-315, 341-342. This follow-up covers publication coherence, affected-workspace selection, and successful retry notification without unnecessary refurnish. No repair is authorized now.
design: Design is pending the Mind beliefNexus Primary and is judged after first-launch priorities. Model one repository revision change as one candidate snapshot, derive affected workspaces from the modules each workspace actually consumes, publish each affected workspace atomically, and emit the coherent typed result only for successful publications. A recovered retry must retain the originating repository and changed-module basis. Do no repair until the Primary selects the event and partial-failure semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic executable proof furnishes workspace A from a changed module, workspace B from an unchanged module in the same repository, and workspace C from another repository. After the source change, only A receives a new publication. One coherent Changed value names the originating repository, exactly the changed modules, and exactly the successfully refurnished workspaces; no preliminary empty-workspace or per-workspace empty-module Changed is emitted. Forced publication failure omits that workspace from success notification and records typed failure. After restart, a successful retry emits the same originating repository/module basis exactly once. B and C remain byte- and generation-identical. Retention does not grow for unaffected workspaces. Nix checks pass.
